source.title: Detecting Safety Training Modification in Language Models via Activation Analysis

page_placements.theme: Refusal direction and refusal behaviour under fine-tuning, quantization and uncensoring: drift, compression and dissociation

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some table and figure layout is flattened, but the relevant Table I values and behavioral rates are assignable to models.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures activation geometry and harmful-request compliance across safety-modified models, and reports that behavioral compliance can change while the measured separation and refusal direction remain intact. This refines the scope of activation-based claims, though it does not perform the original direction-ablation or direction-addition intervention.
record.gate_note: The study computes difference-of-centroids directions and activation-space separation, and measures harmful-prompt compliance. It does not project a direction out of every layer and position, add a direction, or test general capabilities. Its cited descriptions of other work are not recorded as results. Values used only to select layers or thresholds are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study does not run the original ablation or addition interventions. It does measure harmful-request compliance in two released abliterated models against their clean parents, which bears on V2. Its other results use a cluster-separation statistic (σ) on a harmful-vs-benign difference-of-centroids direction, not a refusal rate under intervention. Those are a related construct and are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors propose a four-class taxonomy: training removal, orthogonalization abliteration, rotation-without-collapse abliteration, and behavioral fine-tuning. Tier 1 σ catches classes i–ii and Tier 2 direction similarity catches class iii. Class iv (DarkIdol) evades activation-only probing. Separation predicts compliance directionally but noisily, so AMS must be paired with behavioral evaluation.
record.recipe_differences: The paper computes difference-of-centroids activation directions and pooled-standard-deviation class separation, selecting layers by maximum separation. It does not test the original all-layer, all-position projection-out or direction-addition interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports sensitivity to model and modification category, layer choice, contrastive prompt resampling, threshold-calibration rule, and whether direction similarity is checked against a same-family baseline. It reports that 26 of 42 bootstrap intervals cross the 3.5σ PASS threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: Abliterated models differ in geometry. Llama-abliterated σ fell 5.67→3.33, with direction cosine to its parent as low as 0.30. Gemma-abliterated kept σ 4.54, with cosine 0.70–0.84. Both comply near-fully.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Released abliteration recipes differ in how much harmful/harmless separation and direction they leave intact, while both removing refusal.

fits_no_version.finding: DarkIdol, an uncensored fine-tune, keeps σ 4.01–5.45 across layers and keeps its direction, yet complies with 97% of prompts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal behavior can be removed by fine-tuning while the harmful-vs-harmless mid-layer direction stays intact.

fits_no_version.finding: Base models and Dolphin fine-tunes show low harmful/benign separation (0.48–1.38σ) and high compliance. Across 14 models, separation correlates with compliance at r=−0.546 (Spearman not significant).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful/harmless activation separation is weaker in models without safety training and predicts compliance only noisily.

record.problems: The validation set contains 14 model configurations and relatively few distinct modification procedures. Behavioral evaluation uses 20 prompts per model and a refusal-phrase string-match heuristic. Bootstrap intervals are wide, the separation estimator has reported upward bias, and threshold calibration and evaluation use the same model set. The paper itself cautions that the results are exploratory and do not establish population-level error rates.
record.rows_left_out: No additional per-model main results from Table I were left out. The paper also reports a separate quantization validation and threshold-sensitivity analysis; these were not extracted because they do not test the listed claim versions. Per-layer plots are summarized only where the text gives explicit ranges or aggregate values.

untested.parts: No projection-out, no direction addition, no capability check.
The paper performs no weight edit itself, and the capability retention of the abliterated models is not measured.
Harm judgment and refusal decision are not measured separately.
Removability of a direction is never tested as a function of training. The base and Dolphin results concern separation only.

missing.what: Table V reports base Gemma-2-9b at 5.29σ (PASS) and base Qwen2.5-7B at 2.75σ, plus Lexi-Uncensored at 1.08σ and LLama-3-8b-Uncensored at 1.06σ. These are absent from the rows and from the 14-model set. Gemma base contradicts the claim that 'training removal collapses' separation.
At each model's natural layer: Llama σ 5.67→2.42 after abliteration (cos 0.55); Gemma σ 4.70→4.01 (cos 0.83).

record.verdict_notes: This is a detection-tool paper. Its 'refusal direction' is a final-token difference of centroids over 16 author-written pairs, at the layer that maximizes separation. It is not the original intervention. Only the abliterated-model compliance rates bear on a version (V2). The record's V7 links over-read separation as evidence about removable directions. LOOCV accuracy is the study's own method performance. The behavioral classifier is a first-250-character refusal string match over 20 prompts.

versions.untested_parts: No causal projection-out or direction-addition intervention; no test that refusal is removed or induced by those interventions; no measurement of whether other abilities remain intact.
The paper evaluates released abliterated models but does not itself perform a weight edit. It does not assess general capability costs.
No test of jailbreak attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
The paper reports direction shifts and preserved geometry, but does not test whether refusal is better represented by an affine set, cone, or dominant direction plus other directions.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No cross-language or base-to-instruct transfer test.
The study compares existing model and modification categories, but does not control or vary the timing or protocol of safety training in a prospective experiment.

labels.reason: Table I: compliance rose from 0.57 to 0.93 (mlabonne Llama) and from 0.05 to 1.00 (IlyaGusev Gemma), so refusal is near-fully removed in both. The study is not an original source for V2. Caveats: n=20, string-match classifier, no uncertainty on compliance.

relation.reason: Its own Table I compliance rates for released abliterated models against their parents bear on V2.

tranche.reason: The paper's main method is a detector that uses difference-of-centroids directions as a tool. Separately, it measures compliance of two third-party released abliterated checkpoints against their clean parents. That is a new setting with a result on V2, so T3 fits. Nothing in it argues that a version is wrong or needs restating, so T5 is not supported.

source_check.notes: The compliance classifier looks lenient: the clean Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct already scores 0.57. Several rates (0.57, 0.93, 0.97, 0.38) are not multiples of 1/20, so PARTIAL responses are probably given partial credit, but the text never says so. Base-model σ (0.69, 0.48 vs 5.67 and 8.37 for instruct) and the DarkIdol and Gemma 'separation kept, refusal gone' results are non-causal separation statistics with an upward-biased estimator. Leaving them unlinked to V5, V6 and V7 is defensible. Single-author tool paper by a Google employee.

statements.correction: Checkpoints: mlabonne/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-abliterated (standard FailSpy orthogonalization) and IlyaGusev/gemma-2-9b-it-abliterated (modified recipe with embedding-layer rescaling). Compliance: 20 stratified JailbreakBench prompts, 9 categories, greedy decoding, max 256 tokens. Classifier: refusal-phrase string match on the first 250 characters, spot-checked only. No CI on compliance; bootstrap CIs are on σ only. Clean Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct parent already at 0.57 compliance.
statements.problem: The 0.57->0.93 and 0.05->1.00 numbers are right. But the conditions list of checkpoint sources leaves out IlyaGusev, who made the Gemma checkpoint. And the 'uncertainty' credited to this study covers only the σ bootstrap CIs; the cited compliance rates have none.

statements.correction: DarkIdol σharmful 4.01-5.45 across the 20-90% depth band (Section VII-F); 5.45 at the selected layer (Table I). Compliance 0.97 on 20 JailbreakBench prompts by string match; the text also says 19 of 20. Parent Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct: σ 5.67, compliance 0.57. Direction preservation has no reported cosine (DarkIdol is absent from Table II and Fig. 3).
statements.problem: Correct as the paper states it. But direction preservation is only asserted (Table III 'Preserved (intact)'); no DarkIdol cosine value is reported. The paper's own '19 of 20' equals 95%, not 97%.
